newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian business chief escapes bomb attack.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian business chief escapes bomb attack.

text.p: A powerful bomb apparently aimed at the head of one of Bulgaria's biggest business conglomerates wrecked his car on a mountain road outside Sofia early on Tuesday but no one was hurt, state radio said.
The bomb, planted in the road, exploded around 1 a.m. as two Multigroup cars were driving along the road between Sofia and a company hotel in the nearby village of Bistritsa.
Multigroup President Ilia Pavlov, a former member of the national wrestling team, was not in either of the cars. His armoured BMW was badly damaged.
A Reuters photographer who went to the scene said the blast produced a crater seven metres (20 feet) long and three metres (10 feet) deep, blew down trees and shattered the windows of nearby villas.

Multigroup is the most successful of a handful of Bulgarian firms set up in the legal and administrative chaos that followed the collapse of communist rule in 1989 and has sometimes attracted negative publicity.
Car bombs are frequently used by the Balkan country's rival business groups to settle scores.
Pavlov's office declined to comment on the explosion.
